newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmaker urges reprisals against U.S.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmaker urges reprisals against U.S.

text.p: A ruling party lawmaker said on Monday Colombia should take reprisals against U.S. interests in the country if Washington imposes economic sanctions.
Sanctions could be announced as early as Thursday when the Clinton administration will report whether Colombia has been "certified" as a trustworthy ally in the anti-drug fight.

President Bill Clinton stopped short of imposing sanctions when Colombia was "decertified" for the first time last year. They could include the elimination of tariff preferences enjoyed by Colombian exporters.

Sen. Amilkar Acosta of President Ernesto Samper's Liberal Party said he and other lawmakers had drafted a bill that would allow Samper to seize extraordinary powers and take unspecified action against U.S. interests throughout Colombia if Washington moves to cripple the local economy.
Colombians "shouldn't let ourselves be caught with our pants down in the face of whatever decision the U.S. government eventually takes," Acosta told reporters.

It was not immediately clear when his emergency legislation would go before Congress but he said it was aimed at ensuring the country could respond in kind if its economy were punished for the government's perceived failures in the fight against drugs.

"For every measure that the United States adopts affecting the country's economy, the Colombian government ought to respond in kind with respect to U.S. interests in Colombia," he said. "We're talking about investments and exports," he added.

Samper told Reuters this month that sanctions would be "highly demoralising" and fuel growing anti-American sentiment in Colombia. But he stopped short of saying he would take reprisals if sanctions were imposed.
